# Shortest Path Traversing All Edges in K₁₄

## Identifying the Problem

This is the **Chinese Postman Problem**: finding the shortest closed walk that traverses every edge at least once.

## Graph Properties of K₁₄

- **Number of vertices:** $n = 14$
- **Number of edges:** $\frac{n(n-1)}{2} = \frac{14 \times 13}{2} = 91$
- **Degree of each vertex:** $n - 1 = 13$ (odd)
- **Edge weight:** 1 (all equal)

## Total Weight of All Edges

$$W_{\text{edges}} = 91 \times 1 = 91$$

## Making the Graph Eulerian

An Eulerian circuit exists if and only if every vertex has even degree. Since all 14 vertices have degree 13 (odd), I must duplicate edges to make all degrees even.

**Pairing the odd-degree vertices:** I need to pair up all 14 vertices into 7 pairs, duplicating the shortest path between each pair.

Since K₁₄ is a **complete graph** (every vertex is directly connected to every other), the shortest path between any two vertices is simply **one edge** (weight = 1).

**Minimum matching cost:**
$$\text{7 pairs} \times 1 = 7$$

## Computing the Total Length

$$\text{Total} = W_{\text{edges}} + W_{\text{duplicated}} = 91 + 7 = 98$$

## Verification
- After duplicating 7 edges (one per pair), each of the 14 vertices gains +1 degree → degree becomes 14 (even) ✓
- The resulting multigraph is Eulerian, so an Eulerian circuit exists ✓
- The circuit traverses all 91 original edges plus 7 duplicated edges ✓

$$\boxed{98}$$
